title: A tech expo
scene: Anna helps at a tech expo. The keynote speaker is a famous businesswoman and a product manager; sponsors hang banners, a promoter hands out flyers about a bestseller, the PR team sends a press release, and a speaker explains email marketing and a good landing page.

The CEO gave the keynote at the conference.
The product manager decides which features to build.
The bank is the main sponsor of the race.
A big banner hung above the school entrance.
The concert promoter sold all the tickets.
They handed out flyers on the street.
Her first novel became a bestseller.
The company sent out a press release about the new phone.
My sister has worked in high-tech for ten years.
She wants to find a job in high tech.
I have a movie poster on my bedroom wall.
There is a big billboard on the highway.

old_story: Last weekend, Anna helped her friend at a big tech [[expo]] in Kyiv. The [[keynote]] was given by a famous [[businesswoman]] who started as a [[product manager]]. Every [[sponsor]] hung a bright [[banner]] above its stand. At the door, a young [[promoter]] handed Anna a [[flyer]] about a new book. The book, about smart robots, was already a [[bestseller]]. The [[PR]] team sent a [[press release]] to all the news sites at noon. Anna went to a short talk about [[email marketing]] for small shops. The speaker said she had worked in [[high-tech]] for twenty years. The most popular stand had an [[android]] that looked almost human. It smiled, shook Anna's hand and said, "Welcome to the future!" That evening, Anna told Max she wanted a job in [[high tech]] one day.

title: Uncle Oleh, the trader
scene: Anna's uncle is a trader at a big bank. He explains trading and a broker's work at a brokerage, the stock market index and dividends, buys bitcoin, follows the smart money, and talks about futures, derivatives, hedge funds and asset management.

words.ex: He works as a trader on Wall Street.
He works in stock trading at a big bank.
My broker bought shares for me.
He opened an account at an online brokerage.
The stock market index went up again today.
The company pays a dividend every quarter.
He bought some bitcoin five years ago.
Many traders try to follow the smart money in the market.
He trades oil futures on the market.
He trades derivatives at a big bank in London.
He works as a manager at a hedge fund.
My sister works in asset management at a big bank.
A broker-dealer buys and sells stocks for its clients.

old_story: Anna's uncle Oleh works as a [[trader]] at a big bank in Kyiv. At Sunday lunch, Anna asked him what [[trading]] really is. "I buy and sell shares for people, a bit like a [[broker]]," he said. "You can open your own account at a [[brokerage]] with very little money." He showed her the stock market [[index]] on his phone. "This company pays me a [[dividend]] every quarter," he smiled. Then he admitted that he also bought some [[bitcoin]] last year. "Most people just try to follow the [[smart money]]," he added. He also explained oil [[futures]] and a strange [[derivative]] that nobody at the table understood. His old friend now runs a [[hedge fund]] in London. Anna laughed and said she would study [[asset management]], starting with her pocket money.

title: The economy on TV
scene: An economist on TV talks about a boom and a collapse, the budget deficit, debts of a trillion dollars, the fall of the ruble and a country close to default; an insider talks about a drug cartel's money, risk management at banks, a broker-dealer and tax-free shopping at the airport.

words.ex: The economist predicts a slow year.
There is a boom in online shopping right now.
The economy is close to collapse after the war.
The country has a large budget deficit.
The country's debt is over a trillion dollars.
The country is close to default on its debt.
An insider told reporters about the secret plan.
She works in risk management at an insurance company.
You can buy tax-free goods at the airport.
Kyiv has about three million people.

old_story: Anna and Max were watching the evening news at Max's flat. An [[economist]] in a blue jacket talked about a [[boom]] in online shopping. "But some small shops are close to [[collapse]]," she warned. Then she explained what a budget [[deficit]] is, using a simple chart. "Some countries owe more than a [[trillion]] dollars," she said. Max's grandpa laughed and took an old [[ruble]] coin out of his pocket. "When a country cannot pay its debts, we call it [[default]]," the economist continued. Next, a bank [[insider]] told reporters how a drug [[cartel]] tried to hide its money. Thanks to good [[risk management]], the bank stopped them in time. After that, a [[broker-dealer]] gave tips about buying and selling stocks. Anna yawned and changed the channel to an ad for [[tax-free]] shopping at the airport. "That's the only economy I understand," Max joked.

title: A party for the rich
scene: Max's rich cousin takes him to a cocktail party with a burlesque show. He meets a self-made millionaire, an oil magnate with a huge conglomerate and business interests everywhere, people from show business who talk about the box office and eat caviar, and a man who gives an endowment to a university.

words.ex: We are invited to a cocktail party on Friday.
We saw a burlesque show in a small club.
My uncle is a self-made businessman from a small town.
He became a millionaire before he turned thirty.
The oil magnate bought a new yacht.
The company is part of a large conglomerate.
He has business interests in three countries.
The movie was a big hit at the box office.
We tried black caviar at the party.
The university has a large endowment.
The hotel hosted a big wedding banquet.
She wore a long dress to the gala.

old_story: Max's rich cousin Denys invited him to a [[cocktail party]] in a fancy hotel. The evening started with a funny old-style [[burlesque]] show with songs and jokes. Denys introduced Max to a [[self-made]] businessman from a small village. The man became a [[millionaire]] before he turned thirty. Next to him stood an oil [[magnate]] who owned a huge [[conglomerate]]. "I have [[business interests|business interest]] in five countries," he told Max proudly. A group of actors from [[show business]] were discussing their new movie. "It did great at the [[box office]]," one actress said, eating [[caviar]] on tiny crackers. Later, a quiet old man gave a big [[endowment]] to the university where Max studies. Max decided that was the most impressive thing he saw all night.
